skill.name: api-mitmproxy
skill.description: Guides authorized API security testing with mitmproxy, including HTTPS traffic inspection, request modification, replay, scripting, mobile testing, and HAR export.
skill.summary: Use mitmproxy to inspect, modify, replay, and document authorized API traffic tests.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, public reference links, or educational security templates. Confirmed risks include a curl-to-shell CI installer, GitHub token exposure in a third-party action context, broad proxy binding, proxy environment variables, and an active path traversal payload. Semantic review also found dual-use credential capture, certificate pinning bypass, and WebSocket tampering guidance; no prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Remote installer piped directly to shell in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned package, verified checksum, or reviewed release artifact before execution.

remediation.issue: Proxy examples bind to all interfaces and set global proxy variables.
remediation.suggestion: Default to localhost, document firewall requirements, scope proxy variables to one command, and unset them after tests.

remediation.issue: Examples capture tokens and demonstrate bypass or tampering techniques.
remediation.suggestion: Add stronger authorization warnings, redact token output, avoid storing secrets, and require isolated test environments.

content.value_statement: API teams need controlled visibility into encrypted client traffic during authorized tests. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through mitmproxy workflows for inspection, replay, scripting, and HAR export.
actual_capabilities: Explains mitmproxy, mitmweb, and mitmdump modes for API traffic inspection.
Guides flow recording, replay, and HAR export for security review.
Shows Python addon patterns for authentication tests, parameter fuzzing, GraphQL, and WebSockets.
Covers mobile proxy setup, CA certificate installation, and certificate pinning test context.
Includes CI/CD and rule template assets for security scanning workflows.
limitations: Requires mitmproxy and permission to intercept the target traffic.
Does not replace a complete API vulnerability scanner or manual review.
Examples need adaptation for each application, protocol, and test environment.
Captured traffic can contain secrets and personal data that require protection.

use_cases.title: Test Mobile API Traffic
use_cases.description: Capture and review HTTPS requests from an authorized mobile test device.

use_cases.title: Debug API Integrations
use_cases.description: Inspect request headers, responses, and replay behavior in a staging environment.

use_cases.title: Automate Proxy-Based Checks
use_cases.description: Plan mitmdump workflows that record flows and support repeatable security checks.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an API Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an authorized staging API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect HTTPS API traffic for an authorized staging app. Include setup steps, capture goals, and reporting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Mobile Proxy Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mobile API testing checklist using mitmproxy. Include CA certificate handling, device proxy settings, and data protection steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Automated Replay Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate traffic replay and regression testing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized mitmdump workflow to capture API flows, replay them safely, and summarize security observations.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Addon Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before running custom interception scripts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a proposed mitmproxy addon design for risks. Focus on credential handling, request modification, logging, and cleanup controls.

output_examples.input: Inspect traffic from a staging mobile app during an authorization test.
output: A test plan covering proxy setup, CA certificate trust, and target scope.
A review checklist for tokens, object identifiers, and privilege boundaries.
A reporting outline that separates evidence, impact, and remediation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a HAR export review for an API regression test.
output_examples.output: The result describes capture timing, sensitive-field redaction, replay limits, and findings to include in the final report.

output_examples.input: Review risks before setting proxy variables in CI.
output_examples.output: The result identifies credential exposure risks, recommends scoped environment variables, and adds cleanup steps after the test job.

best_practices: Use the skill only for systems where interception is approved in writing.
Bind proxies to localhost unless remote devices require a controlled test network.
Redact tokens, cookies, and personal data before storing or sharing captures.
anti_patterns: Do not intercept production traffic without explicit authorization and data handling controls.
Do not commit flow files, HAR files, certificates, or captured tokens to source control.
Do not leave proxy environment variables active after the test session ends.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and run authorized mitmproxy workflows for API traffic inspection, replay, scripting, and reporting.

faq.question: Does it install mitmproxy for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but the user must install and run mitmproxy tools.

faq.question: Can I use it on production systems?
faq.answer: Use production traffic only with explicit authorization, strict data controls, and approved change windows.

faq.question: How should I handle captured secrets?
faq.answer: Redact secrets immediately, restrict access to captures, and delete temporary files after the test.

faq.question: Does it support mobile app testing?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes mobile proxy setup guidance and certificate trust considerations.

faq.question: Is this a complete vulnerability scanner?
faq.answer: No. It is a workflow guide for traffic analysis and should be paired with manual review and other tools.
